content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

I'd love to help you build this. Before anything technical, I want to make sure I understand what you're really after, so we build the right thing.

Let me start with the "why":

**When your bookmark app is finished and working well, what would be different about your day compared to now?** For example — are you frustrated with losing links you meant to come back to? Drowning in browser bookmarks you can never find again? Wanting to share collections with other people? Something else?

And a quick follow-up when you're ready: **who is this for — just you, or other people too?**

There are no wrong answers here — I just want to hear it in your own words so we aim at the real goal rather than my guess of it. Once I understand the point of it, I'll show you working screens you can actually click through, one flow at a time, rather than making you read specifications.

It’s mainly for me. I save lots of links intending to return to them, but they disappear into a messy browser bookmark list and become hard to find.

I’d like one personal place where I can quickly save a link, organise it, find it again by searching, and keep track of what I still want to read. I’d also like to archive things I want to keep without cluttering the main view. Sharing and multiple users aren’t priorities.

That's really clear, thank you. Let me play back what I understood to make sure I've got the direction right:

> The problem isn't saving links — browsers already do that. It's that saved links become a **messy pile you can't find your way back through**. What you want is **one personal place** where you can:
> - quickly capture a link,
> - organise it so it doesn't turn into a pile,
> - find it again by searching,
> - track what you still intend to read (vs. what you're done with),
> - and tuck away things you want to keep long-term without cluttering the main view.
>
> Just for you. Sharing and multiple accounts are not the point.

If I had to name the *real* goal in one line, it'd be: **"Links I save actually get found and read again, instead of disappearing."** Does that capture it — and is there anything I've overstated or missed?

One thing I want to check on so I present it the right way: **what kind of app do you picture using?** For example something you open in your **web browser**, a **mobile** app on your phone, a **desktop** app, or a **command-line** tool? If you have a preference I'll build around it; if you're not sure, I can suggest one.
Yes, that captures it well. I picture it as a web app I can open in my browser, with a layout that also works comfortably on my phone. I don’t need a separate mobile or desktop app.
